candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: recognize medication adverse effects, provide client education, and monitor therapy appropriately.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — voriconazole visual adverse effects
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize abnormal vision, color-perception changes, and photophobia as labeled voriconazole adverse effects and ensure visual-function monitoring when treatment extends beyond 28 days.

options.A: These are recognized voriconazole-associated visual disturbances; if therapy continues beyond 28 days, visual function should be monitored.
options.B: These findings indicate an expected improvement in visual acuity and require no further assessment.
options.C: These findings prove irreversible blindness and require the nurse to tell the client that vision loss will be permanent.
options.D: These findings are unrelated to voriconazole because the medication has no labeled visual adverse effects.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current DailyMed labeling states that voriconazole-associated visual disturbances are common and can include abnormal vision, color-vision changes, and photophobia. The label also reports prolonged visual adverse reactions such as optic neuritis and papilledema and directs monitoring of visual acuity, visual field, and color perception if treatment continues beyond 28 days. B and D contradict the label. C overstates the prognosis; the label does not say that these symptoms prove permanent blindness, and a controlled 28-day study showed retinal and visual changes returning to normal after therapy ended, while prolonged postmarketing events have also been reported.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Voriconazole can cause visual disturbances including abnormal/color vision and photophobia; treatment beyond 28 days requires monitoring of visual function, and visual symptoms should not be characterized as uniformly permanent or benign.
candidate.source_locator: Warnings and Precautions 5.4 Visual Disturbances: prolonged visual reactions including optic neuritis and papilledema have been reported; if treatment continues beyond 28 days, monitor visual acuity, visual field, and color perception. Adverse Reactions — Visual Disturbances: abnormal vision, color-vision change, and photophobia are common treatment-related effects.
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling via DailyMed
candidate.source_version_date: Current DailyMed label updated May 27, 2026; accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: A client receiving voriconazole reports new abnormal color perception and photophobia. Which interpretation by the nurse is most accurate?
